spec_match.rationale: Draws the same foreignObject SVG from http:, data: and blob: sources onto fresh canvases and reads each back with getImageData(), which is the exact origin-clean contract the Chrome 156 change modifies, with a no-foreignObject control isolating the rule from the scheme.

interactive.rationale: Run builds three brand-new canvases (correctly, since taint is permanent), performs real draws and readbacks, paints per-cell verdicts from the actual SecurityError, and fills the 'this browser' column of the engine table from observations.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card says the verdicts are read from real SecurityErrors, not a typed table, and that a pre-156 browser will report the blob column tainted — which is exactly what this Chromium 141 session's conformance run confirmed.

edge_cases.rationale: Fresh-canvas-per-run, the plain-SVG control, and the image-load failure branch are all handled, but the control run silently substitutes a data: URI for the http: cell, and a load failure is painted with the 'tainted' verdict/style even though nothing was drawn.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5196074156032000 and the HTML Standard canvas-security section.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite covers the changed contract, a data: control, a plain-SVG blob control and the export path, with async assertions the runner properly awaits; on Chromium 141 it ran 4 pass / 2 fail — precisely the pre-156 split (both blob foreignObject assertions failing) — and the shared support panel renders on the page.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): desktop and true-360 mobile screenshots read, DOM dumped, console clean ('[foreignobject-taint:matrix] ready'), fixture.svg served 200, and the /conformance/ route exercised the same draw/readback contract live — but the Run button itself is click-driven and could not be pressed headlessly, so the matrix stayed at 'not run' in captures.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert reports 'taint-matrix-run' with the per-scheme outcomes and the foreignObject flag, and load produces no console or network errors.

design_system.rationale: All styling uses design-system variables and buttons override background and color, but the .cell.clean verdict uses --accent-emerald (#0a8f5c) on --bg-stone (~3.7:1), short of WCAG AA for its 0.85rem bold text — the shared palette shortfall also noted on the v156 @property pages.

accessibility.rationale: The run summary lands in an aria-live=polite output, the engine table has a caption and row/column th scoping, verdicts pair text with the aria-hidden icon, and the control checkbox sits inside its label with a 44px hit area.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at true 360px and 1280px: the three cells stack to one column on mobile with canvases scaling to width, the engine table fits, and there is no horizontal overflow or clipped control on either class.

openQuestions.title: Control run's http: cell actually tests a data: URI
openQuestions.detail: When 'include the foreignObject' is unticked, httpSource falls back to a data: URI (there is no plain-SVG fixture), yet the cell is still headed 'http: (same origin)' and the summary sentence reports 'http clean' as if a network fetch had been tested. Add a fixture-plain.svg next to fixture.svg and load it over http in the control run, or label the cell honestly ('data: stand-in') when the substitution happens — a probe must test what its label claims (build rule 7 / anti-regression 'false support probe').

openQuestions.title: Image-load failure is painted as 'tainted'
openQuestions.detail: The catch branch around load() sets outcome.state to 'tainted' with why-text 'The image never loaded'. The rose styling and the verdict word then claim a taint verdict for a canvas that was never drawn to, and the obs- table cell records 'tainted' into the engine-comparison row. A third 'error' state (neutral styling, excluded from the table) would keep the matrix honest when a load fails.

openQuestions.title: Emerald 'clean' verdict text misses WCAG AA on stone
openQuestions.detail: --accent-emerald (#0a8f5c) on --bg-stone is ~3.7:1, below 4.5:1 for the 0.85rem bold verdict text. Same shared-palette finding as the other v156 pages this pass reviewed; likely wants one palette-level decision.

summary: A well-constructed matrix demo whose verdicts genuinely come from drawImage + getImageData rather than a hardcoded table, with fresh canvases per run and a foreignObject on/off control. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v156/svg-foreignobject-does-not-taint-the-canvas-for-blob-urls/taint-matrix/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots, DOM dump, clean console, fixture.svg 200). The Run click could not be driven headlessly, but the feature /conformance/ route executes the identical contract and returned 4 pass / 2 fail — the expected pre-156 result on this 141 build, matching the page's own engine table for Chrome <= 155. Two honesty gaps to close: the control run substitutes a data: URI while the cell still says http:, and a load failure borrows the 'tainted' verdict.
